item.title: CapCut Launches Seedance AI Video Generation Tool for Windows
item.description:
CapCut Launches Seedance AI Video Generation Tool for Windows

CapCut has introduced CapCut Seedance, a new AI video generation tool built for Windows that turns text prompts and still images into short motion clips. Designed to integrate directly into the CapCut video pipeline, the tool allows generated clips to flow straight into a familiar editing timeline.

🔍 Overview

CapCut Seedance is designed for both beginners who want to produce social-ready footage without prior editing experience, and professionals who need fast concept previews or b-roll drafts before committing to a full production. Within the platform, the model provides raw motion while the editor gives users control over timing, framing, and delivery. The workflow is built to be iterative, allowing creators to quickly regenerate variations instead of rebuilding a project from scratch. Additionally, the community around CapCut tutorials, prompt-sharing threads, and template packs continues to expand as the underlying models evolve with each release.

🧩 How it works

The workspace offers several features that streamline the process of generating and editing AI video assets:

  • Text-to-Video generation: Describe a scene in plain language to generate a short clip that follows the prompt.
  • Image-to-Video animation: Bring still images to life with controlled camera moves, parallax, and subtle object motion, which is useful for product shots, portraits, and archival stills.
  • Motion presets: Access a library of ready-made motion patterns (such as pans, zooms, orbits, and drift) that can be applied with one click and tuned for intensity and direction.
  • Prompt helper: Built-in helpers suggest richer wording for prompts, including lighting, lens, and mood cues.
  • Visual reference: Use a still frame as a visual reference so generated clips inherit its color palette, grain, and composition feel.
  • Aspect ratio presets: Generate vertical, square, or widescreen output, with common presets for social platforms to avoid manual reframing.
  • Seed comparison: Queue multiple generations of the same prompt with different seeds and compare them side by side.
  • Direct timeline integration: Generated clips drop into the CapCut editing timeline with basic metadata intact, allowing users to trim, layer audio, add captions, and export without leaving the editor ecosystem.

⚙️ Key details

To run CapCut Seedance on Windows, your system must meet the following technical requirements:

Specification Minimum Requirement Recommended Requirement
Operating System Windows 10, Windows 11 Windows 10, Windows 11
Architecture x64 x64
Processor Intel Core i5 (10th gen or newer) or AMD Ryzen 5 equivalent Intel Core i7 or AMD Ryzen 7
RAM 8 GB 16 GB or more
Storage 4 GB for installation + 10 GB for clips and cache 4 GB for installation + 10 GB or more (faster storage recommended)
Dependencies DirectX 11 or newer, Visual C++ Redistributable, current GPU driver with hardware video encoding support Discrete GPU with at least 6 GB of video memory and a recent driver

Generation and rendering lean heavily on GPU acceleration. Running the tool near the minimum specifications may lead to longer generation times, reduced preview quality, and occasional stalls on larger image inputs, though it remains usable for short clips. Pairing CapCut Seedance with a discrete GPU and faster storage improves performance and shortens cache writes when generating multiple variations.

item.title: Adobe Expands Creative Cloud with New AI Editing Tools
item.description:
Adobe Expands Creative Cloud with New AI Editing Tools

Adobe announced new AI capabilities for Creative Cloud apps and its Firefly platform at the Max event, aiming to speed up design and editing tasks.

🔍 Overview

  • Adobe is expanding Creative Cloud apps and Firefly AI platform with new capabilities.
  • Announcements include automatic removal of objects, blemishes, and distractions in Premiere, Photoshop, and Lightroom, plus new generative AI tools and collaborative experiences.

🧩 How it works

  • Premiere Generative Remove (beta)
    • Mask an object, click Remove; Premiere fills the area with realistic detail using generative AI while surrounding footage stays untouched.
  • Photoshop updated Remove Tool
    • Better at detecting and reconstructing surrounding elements such as reflections, shadows, and footprints.
  • Photoshop Quick Compare
    • Before‑and‑after split‑screen slider to review changes without switching layers.
  • Photoshop Relight
    • Add and position new light sources to dynamically adjust hue and brightness.
  • Lightroom blemish removal
    • Single‑tap skin retouch on desktop (previously mobile only).
  • Lightroom Open Eyes (public beta)
    • Replaces closed eyes with natural‑looking open eyes using a reference photo from the library.
  • Premiere new sound editing tools
    • Clean messy recordings and separate dialogue, music, ambience, and sound effects into individual tracks.
  • Firefly Quick Actions
    • Ready‑to‑use workflows for creating video thumbnails and product ads, now generally available.
  • Firefly Design
    • Combined space for illustration, image editing, animation, 3D, and print (beta).
  • Firefly Graph
    • Helps creators build and iterate on custom, repeatable workflows.
  • Firefly Builder (private beta)
    • Tool for prototyping websites and apps.

⚙️ Key details

  • Generative Media tool introduced earlier this year is now generally available.
  • Color Mode color editing experience, launched in beta in April, is now generally available.
  • Features are part of Adobe’s broader expansion of Creative Cloud and Firefly AI platform.

🚀 Availability

  • Premiere Generative Remove – beta.
  • Photoshop Remove Tool – updated now.
  • Photoshop Quick Compare and Relight – newly added.
  • Lightroom blemish removal – coming to desktop.
  • Lightroom Open Eyes – public beta.
  • Firefly Quick Actions – generally available.
  • Firefly Design, Graph – beta; Firefly Builder – private beta.
  • Generative Media and Color Mode – generally available.

#Adobe #CreativeCloud #AI #VideoEditing

Source: Photoshop, Lightroom, and Premiere are making it easier to remove things

item.title: Adobe Updates Premiere Pro with New Generative Media and AI Audio Tools
item.description:
Adobe Updates Premiere Pro with New Generative Media and AI Audio Tools

Adobe is overhauling how editors interact with AI in its Premiere professional video editing software, introducing a dedicated interface for generative media directly within the project timeline.

🧩 How it works

Editors can now highlight an empty gap on video or audio tracks to generate content without leaving the software. The new Generative Media tool allows for the creation of video, sound effects, music, and soundscapes, eliminating the need to use browsers or external applications to source missing assets.

⚙️ Key details

Editors can select from several underlying models directly within the timeline to suit specific project styles:

Model Name Capability
Adobe Firefly Generative Media
Google Veo Generative Media
Runway Generative Media
Luma Generative Media
Kling Generative Media

🎙️ New AI Audio Capabilities

Premiere is receiving new AI-powered audio tools in beta, including:

  • Separation of overlapping speakers.
  • Automatic music ducking under speech.
  • Independent adjustment of dialogue and ambience.

🛠️ After Effects Integration

Adobe is also bringing its AI Assistant to After Effects in beta. This feature supports plain-language commands to help editors organize projects, fix technical issues, and create effects without the manual use of expressions.

#Adobe #PremierePro #GenerativeAI #VideoEditing #AfterEffects

Source: Adobe is trying to make its AI generators idiot-proof in Premiere
